data.name: A House of Many Doors
data.detailed_description:
Welcome to the House. You are not welcome.

Explore the House, a parasite dimension that steals from other worlds, in a train that scuttles on mechanical legs.

Uncover secrets. Open locked doors. Lead a crew of dysfunctional characters. Write procedurally-generated poems. Fight in turn-based combat. Explore a strange new setting, dripping with atmosphere, crusted with lore. Escape. Escape. Escape.

You are an explorer, poet and spy, launching yourself into the unknown in search of adventure. Rig an election in the city of the dead. Visit a village lit by the burning corpse of a god (careful not to inhale the holy smoke). Sell your teeth to skittering spider-things for a moment in their library. Over 90 bizarre locations await discovery in the dust and the dark.

A House of Many Doors is a 2D exploration RPG that takes inspiration from Sunless Sea, China Mieville, Planescape: Torment and Italo Calvino's Invisible Cities. It features over 300,000 words of branching original story and over 770 trillion bad poems.

WARNING.

Please be aware that this game contains the following romance options:
  • Men.
  • Women.
  • Goatman.
  • Ten million crows.
  • An oil rig.

A House of Many Doors has benefited from the kind support and partial funding of Failbetter Games, makers of Sunless Sea and Fallen London.

reviews.review:
Don't play it. Just watch it somewhere.
What an absolute shame, because the worldbuilding and characters are so wonderful and it certainly would have been more fun to experience it in an immersive roleplaying way, making my own choices. But the gameplay is SO intolerable it drags down any fun that might have had. The only way I could possibly endure it is via some other brave soul struggling through the tedium and recording it for us weaker-willed mortals...

The resolution options are bizarrely small, the font is hard to read, it crashes all the time and does a weird thing where it says its still running but you can never reopen the window. Lost my first hour of play to that cos I couldn't find where the save option is!
You start the game by selecting if you want a tutorial, being confused that none appears, finally figuring out the tiny ? icons popping randomly around the screen are supposedly that. The only information they manage to provide you is which bizarre object on the screen is your ship, and that you have to struggle through some surreal new variation on WASD where W doesn't mean up. You are then interrupted by a random event telling you your engine died, because a real time system was ticking down throughout that tutorial and you've just doomed all these people through your ignorance. Now get to a town within a time limit while your sanity bar rapidly depletes.

Getting to this town is five screens of just hitting accelerate in a straight line, with no interactable events. What is the reason to even make you manually pilot this thing, what is the reason for the terrain being randomly generated? You can't do a single thing with it. These may as well be plain white rooms that you slap a single button to escape.
Along the way you might want to bond with your crewmembers, but you don't get a choice in that since half the cast refuses to even introduce yourself unless you have 15 Apprehensions, something which also hasn't been explained. You get to the town, in which zero tutorials appear. An overwhelming amount of seemingly random items sit in the shop menu, providing zero information as to their function. Wondering if they're trade goods, you purchase one single log, and find it sells for exactly the same amount in every other town in existance.
All those towns are also through 5-15 blank featureless rooms.

You finally encounter a rival ship! Every negotiation option fails, because you genuinely have no clue where your stat screen is or how the hell to gain Guile. You are now thrown into the most confusing combat screen I have ever seen, where you control dozens of people simultaneously to manually walk to the engine room, etc. The tutorial tells you nothing but how to end your turn. Attempting to click around and figure it out wastes some action points that you didn't know you had, and the enemy blasts you in the face. It takes several more turns to find out how to even attack at all, and you are summarily told that you died despite not a single character's HP bar being under 50%.

You still don't know how to save.

So yeah uhh.. watch a lets play, guys. I'd love to be immersed in this world but I ain't getting much luck when I can barely wrangle basic controls. 
This feels like the creator was forced to add "actual gameplay" with no idea how to program it. It would be SO much better as a visual novel! If you ever make a remake like that, call me up cos I'd be stoked to continue befriending the sad alcoholic grandpa hunting for doctors who steal hearts. INSTANTLY so invested in his plotline!
